text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Thursday:

- Some 10,000 Swiss farmers protested against the Swiss government's agriculture policy in Berne on Wedensday. As several young farmers tried to cross a fence to get access to the house of parliament, the police used rubber bullets and tear gas to stop the demonstrants.
- Swiss television reported that Foreign Minister Flavio Cotti underwent minor heart surgery in September. The operation was a success, Cotti's surgeon said.

- Swiss Minister for Foreign Affairs Flavio Cotti said yesterday in Berne that the Swiss government would set up two task forces to investigate Switzerland's and its banking sector's role during World War II.
- Inflation rate in Geneva registered a sharp rise in September. Compared to the previous month, the rate rose by 0.3 percentage points to 0.9 percent.
- Several hundred employees of Bally France demonstrated for their job on Wednesday.
- The Swiss government presented its plans to reduce CO2 emmissions by 10 percent until 2010. If this goal cannot be acheived, the government will introduce a special CO2 tax.
